title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'Compléments sur les 2-sous-groupes' section (marked §10 at the top). It is a systematic, invariant-style census of the subgroups of G = S_I, the symmetric group on a 4-element set I, other than e and G. Here the Klein group V ≅ F_2^2 is the normal subgroup of S_I, and V* (its 3 non-trivial elements) is identified with the set P_{2,2}(I) of partitions of I into two pairs. Part A lists the 2-subgroups, i.e. the subgroups lying in a 2-Sylow D ≅ D_4 (dihedral of order 8). The left-margin numbers count the members of each family, and the margin letters (V*, Ṽ*) name the set indexing that family.

Order 2:
- (a) The 3 double transpositions, the elements of V*. They form one Int G-orbit.
- (b) The 6 transpositions, a second orbit. They fall into 3 pairs, indexed by V*, under the relation ττ' ∈ V*. The same pairs arise from the relation 'lying in a common 2-Sylow'. A margin note says equivalently that τ and τ' have the same image in S_3 ≅ S_I/V ≅ GL_2(F_2).

Order 4:
- (c) The 3 cyclic subgroups C_4. They correspond to the 3 'circle structures' (cyclic orders up to reversal) on I and are indexed by V*.
- (d) The normal Klein group V itself (count 1).
- (e) The 3 non-normal Klein groups {e, (ab), (cd), (ab)(cd)}. Each lies in a unique Sylow, which also contains V and one C_4. Together they form one conjugacy class indexed by V*.

Order 8:
- (f) The 3 Sylow subgroups, again indexed by V*.

The next page completes the census: 4 subgroups of order 3, 4 S_3's (point stabilisers) and A_4. That gives 19 + 9 = 28 proper non-trivial subgroups, 30 in all, in 11 conjugacy classes, which Grothendieck reads as 11 isomorphism classes of homogeneous G-spaces.

Purpose: in the context of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, S_I acts on the 4 branch points of x: E → P^1 (equivalently on the 2-torsion data and its 'level' refinements). The quotient S_I/V ≅ S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2) acts on E[2]−{0}. Grothendieck wants a canonical dictionary between subgroups and level-type structures on I (pairings, circle structures, Sylows), presumably to classify the intermediate coverings or quotients of a modular curve, i.e. the homogeneous spaces of G.
errors: No mathematical errors. All counts are correct: 9 subgroups of order 2, 3 + 1 + 3 of order 4, 3 of order 8 (19 two-subgroups ≠ e); with the next page 28 proper non-trivial subgroups and 11 conjugacy classes in total.

Minor imprecision in (e): the garbled parenthetical about the other order-4 subgroups of the Sylow should read 'besides V and the cyclic C_4'. A Sylow D_4 contains exactly three subgroups of order 4: V, one C_4 and one non-normal Klein group.

ideas.what: Complete enumeration of the subgroups of S_4 up to conjugacy (11 classes, 30 subgroups), organised canonically by the sets V* = P_{2,2}(I), circle structures on I, and I itself.
ideas.modern_name: Subgroup lattice of S_4 / table of marks / Burnside ring of S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th-century group theory; standard textbook material)

ideas.what: Identifying the conjugacy classes of subgroups with isomorphism classes of transitive G-sets, and the plan to arrange them in a diagram of morphisms of homogeneous spaces (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Orbit category / Galois correspondence for coverings with group S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Burnside, Galois theory of coverings); in Grothendieck's framework SGA1
ideas.where_published: The general Galois-category viewpoint is in SGA 1, Exp. V; this specific S_4 table is not published

ideas.what: Correspondence between V*, the 2-Sylows, the cyclic subgroups of order 4 and the circle structures on a 4-set, via the quotient S_4 → S_3 = GL_2(F_2).
ideas.modern_name: Exceptional map S_4 → S_3; resolvent cubic / Legendre level-2 structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lagrange/Ferrari resolvent; Legendre form of elliptic curves)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct census of the subgroups of S_4, done in Grothendieck's canonical 'indexing set' style as preparation for classifying level structures and coverings. Nothing here is new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin labels (V*, Ṽ*, I) mark the indexing sets of each family, and the numbers beside them are cardinalities. The '20' at the bottom left is the archive page number, not a count.
In (e) the parenthetical is better read as '(en plus de V, et du cyclique)', i.e. besides V and the cyclic subgroup, rather than 'un plus V, qui est cyclique'.
In (c) the inserted words are likely 'les Sylows' → 'les sous-groupes' (cycliques d'ordre 4), followed by 'i.e. les trois structures de cercle sur I'.
